fields.aka: Kamalākṣa, Kamalākānta Vedapañcānana, Maṅgala, Śrī Advaita Ācārya, Śrī Advaita Prabhu, Kamalākānta Vedapancanana
fields.appearance: Māgha Śukla Saptamī (Advaita Saptamī), 1355 Śaka (1433/1434 CE), at Lāuḍ, Śrīhaṭṭa (Prema-vilāsa: at Śāntipura)
fields.place: Śāntipura; born at Lāuḍ (Śrīhaṭṭa); also Navahaṭṭa, and a house in Navadvīpa; his Deities of Madana-gopāla at Madana-gopāla-pāḍā, Śāntipura
fields.works: Praise of the limbs of Lord Caitanya (pratyaṅga-varṇana-stotra)
fields.notes:
One of the Pañca-tattva; the combined form of Mahā-Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva; «the trunk of the tree of bhakti» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 9.21). His call with Gaṅgā water and tulasī brought Lord Caitanya. Disciple of Mādhavendra Purī. Father Kuvera Paṇḍita (minister of King Divyasiṁha of Lāuḍ), mother Nābhā Devī. Wives Sītā and Śrī, daughters of Nṛsiṁha Bhāḍuḍī, married at Phuliyā. Sons by Sītā: Acyutānanda, Kṛṣṇa Miśra, Gopāla, Balarāma, Svarūpa, Jagadīśa; by Śrī: Śyāmadāsa (Prema-vilāsa 24). Studied under Śānta Ācārya at Phullavatī; met Vidyāpati in Mithilā. Left this world in 1480 Śaka at the age of 125 (Advaita-vilāsa; Advaita-prakāśa 22). His life: Advaita-prakāśa (Īśāna Nāgara), Bālya-līlā-sūtra, Advaita-maṅgala, Advaita-vilāsa, Sītā-caritra.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Sadāśiva (with Mahā-Viṣṇu), who also danced in Vraja as a cowherd boy (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 76-80).

fields.place: Śāntipura and Māyāpura; married at Phuliyā
fields.notes:
Wife of Śrī Advaita Ācārya; daughter of Nṛsiṁha Bhāḍuḍī; sister of Śrī Devī, Advaita's other wife. Named the child Nimāi and brought Him gifts at His birth (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 13); cooked for the Lord at Śāntipura after His sannyāsa and every year in Purī. Sons: Acyutānanda, Kṛṣṇa Miśra, Gopāla Miśra, Balarāma Miśra, Svarūpa Ācārya, Jagadīśa Miśra.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Yogamāyā (Paurṇamāsī); her sister Śrī is Yogamāyā's manifestation (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 86).

Younger wife of Śrī Advaita Ācārya; sister of Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī and daughter of Nṛsiṁha Bhāḍuḍī; married with her sister at Phuliyā. Her son was Śyāmadāsa (Prema-vilāsa 24). When her own newborn son died, Sītā gave her second son Kṛṣṇadāsa (Kṛṣṇa Miśra) to her to bring up (Advaita-prakāśa 11; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: a manifestation (prakāśa) of Yogamāyā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 86).

fields.appearance: 1425 or 1426 Śaka (1503/1504 CE) (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna; B. V. Tīrtha: 1428 Śaka; Digdarśanī: 1414 Śaka)
fields.notes:
Eldest son of Śrī Advaita Ācārya and Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī; disciple of Gadādhara Paṇḍita (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 87-88). As a child of five he rebuked his father for calling Keśava Bhāratī the Lord's guru (Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 4); «Acyuta's view is the essence» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.20). Lived long with the Lord in Purī; at the Kheturī festival. Never married.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Kārttikeya and the gopī Acyutā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 87-88).

fields.name: Kṛṣṇa Miśra (son of Advaita)
fields.notes: Second son of Śrī Advaita Ācārya and Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.18); brought up by Śrī Devī (Advaita-prakāśa 11). Advaita gave him the service of his Deity. Sons Raghunātha (line at Madana-gopāla-pāḍā, Śāntipura) and Dolagovinda (line in Māldaha).

Third son and disciple of Śrī Advaita Ācārya (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.19). Born with his eyes closed, which opened when Advaita called «Gaura Hari». Fainted in ecstasy at the Guṇḍicā cleaning; the Lord revived him (Ādi 12.21-25).

In a past life: Gaṇeśa.

fields.name: Kuvera Paṇḍita
fields.aka: Kuvera Paṇḍit, Kuvera Tarkapañcānana, Kuvera Ācārya
fields.notes:
Father of Śrī Advaita Ācārya. A brāhmaṇa of the Bharadvāja line who kept the agnihotra; minister of King Divyasiṁha of Lāuḍ; wrote the Dattaka-candrikā. Married Nābhā Devī, daughter of Mahānanda Vipra of the Nāḍiyāla family of Navagrāma. Six sons and a daughter (Śrīkānta, Lakṣmīkānta, Hariharānanda, Sadāśiva, Kuśaladāsa, Kīrticandra); the sons went on pilgrimage and four died; the grieving parents moved from Lāuḍ to Śāntipura, and then Advaita was born (Prema-vilāsa 24; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Kuvera, king of the Guhyakas, to whom Sadāśiva promised to be born as his son (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 81-85).

fields.name: Nābhā Devī
fields.notes: Mother of Śrī Advaita Ācārya (Bhakti-ratnākara 12.1756-1758); wife of Kuvera Paṇḍita; daughter of Mahānanda Vipra of the Nāḍiyāla family of Navagrāma (Prema-vilāsa 24). Six sons and a daughter before Advaita; four sons died on pilgrimage.

fields.name: Īśāna Nāgara
fields.notes: Of Advaita's branch. Brought up in Advaita's house from the age of five with his widowed mother. Tore off his sacred thread when the Lord would not let a brāhmaṇa touch His feet. Married at seventy by Sītā Devī's order; sons Puruṣottama Nāgara, Harivallabha and Kṛṣṇavallabha; descendants at Goālanda and Bāṅkpāl near Teotha (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

fields.name: Padmanābha (father of Lokanātha)
fields.notes:
Father of Lokanātha Gosvāmī; a kulīna rāḍhī brāhmaṇa of the Bharadvāja gotra of Tālakhaḍi (Jessore); wife Sītā Devī. As a student he took shelter in Advaita's house at Śāntipura and received dīkṣā from him, and was always absorbed in the Bhāgavatam. Four sons: Bhavanātha, Pūrṇānanda (Pragalbha), Lokanātha and Raghunātha (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Padmanābha Cakravartī»).

This record mixed three persons; the ancestor of Rūpa and Sanātana and Padmanābha Miśra, son of Upendra Miśra, have their own records since 05-11-2026. Same person as Padmanābha Cakravartī (#1884).
